name: Set up wp-env for a WordPress plugin
query: Set up a local WordPress development environment for my plugin so I can run its PHPUnit tests against a real database.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Run wordpress-router to classify repo kind
Step 2: Run wp-project-triage to detect plugin structure and existing tooling
Step 3: Confirm wp-env is the right tool rather than wp-playground (PHPUnit against a real MySQL database)
Step 4: Check Docker is installed and running with docker info
Step 7: If no .wp-env.json exists, confirm auto-detection will find Plugin Name header
Step 8: Install wp-env if not already installed (npm -g install @wordpress/env)
Step 9: Run wp-env start to launch the environment
Step 10: Verify environment is running with wp-env status
Step 11: Confirm plugin appears in WordPress admin with wp-env run cli wp plugin list
success_criteria: wp-env is chosen over wp-playground for a reason listed in the skill (real database needed)
Docker is verified as running before attempting wp-env start
Environment starts successfully on default or configured port
Plugin is auto-detected and mounted in the WordPress instance
Admin dashboard is accessible at the reported URL
No bare plugin slugs used in .wp-env.json (full ZIP URLs for wp.org plugins)
